newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt shakes off consolidation, posts gains.
newsitem.headline: German debt shakes off consolidation, posts gains.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were higher in late dealings, hovering just below new record levels set in earlier trade as the market defied expectations for another bout of consolidation to extend recent gains.

At 1525 GMT, DTB March Bund futures were up 11 basis points at 102.63 but below the new record high set at 102.72 points. The 10-year cash Bund due January 2007 was at 102.81, or a yield of 5.62 percent, up from Friday's close at 102.75.
A lack of fresh fundamentals kept the market focused on technical factors as March futures sought to break resistance at 102.68 in a bid to challenge the 103.00 barrier.
MMS International said in a market commentary that market momentum was "firm at the overbought territory" and a break below 102.30 was necessary for any dip toward 102.00.
In any break below 102.00, chart technicans said they looked for March futures to find support at 101.72 and 101.52.
Dealings on Tuesday were expected to be light due to regional holidays and reflect overnight developments in U.S. debt markets.
